scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep) (E-01).
3025 disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL-read vs 1240 ESTIMATED-read (E-03).
Manual-read route completion at 88% vs 95% target over 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep (E-06).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) despite the volume surge (E-02).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have doubled since August (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to ~1200+/month in Aug-Sep, E-01), primarily because the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are built on reads marked ACTUAL that are themselves wrong — pointing to a fault in the billing import/read-acceptance step rather than in estimate substitution — while a tariff change has been ruled out (E-04, E-03). A smaller share of disputes (1240 of 3025) stems from ESTIMATED-read bills issued when manual-read route completion falls short of target (88% vs 95%, E-06); response-handling throughput is not the bottleneck since response times remain within SLA (E-02).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-03 revised by E-12: E-03 still shows 3025 disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED-read vs 1785 ACTUAL-read; that split and the ACTUAL-read dominance remain valid. It no longer supports that the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes stem from estimate substitution for missing manual reads: E-12 shows 1184 of those 1240 are AMI-channel reads that existed and were received before cutoff but were rejected at billing import under a HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule, so the ESTIMATED-read dispute slice is dominantly an import-validation failure, not a manual-read/route-completion-driven estimate substitution.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling/throughput gap that an AI agent can resolve by auto-answering tickets and auto-fixing bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic errors (e.g., wrongful rejection of valid reads or incorrect estimate substitution) causing a surge of incorrect bills.

H-AMI-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The nightly AMI read export (H-MDMS-BILL) from the vendor-run MDMS began failing or delivering semantically invalid reads, causing bills to be issued on bad or substituted data.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Reduced field reading staffing/capacity caused missed manual meter reads, forcing estimated bills and resulting disputes.

H-TICKET-VOLUME-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets partly reflects a change in CRM categorization, SLA breach re-filing, or ticket counting rather than a doubling of actual billing errors.

H-ACTUAL-READ-DATA-QUALITY.statement: The dominant source of disputes is bills built on reads marked ACTUAL that are themselves wrong (bad import/validation of accepted reads), not estimate substitution for missing reads.

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH.statement: AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) report consumption in 0.1 m3 units while v3.x firmware reports in m3; if billing import fails to rescale v4.2 reads, apparent consumption is inflated ~10x, triggering HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections (E-12) for both ESTIMATED- and ACTUAL-read bills.

H-RULE-FIRMWARE-UNIFIED.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check (deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling: none) misreads raw register values from v4.2-firmware meters (0.1 m3 units, rolled out 2026-06) as ~10x actual consumption, unifying H-RULE-CHANGE and H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH into one root cause behind both ESTIMATED-rejection and potential ACTUAL-read overbilling.

interpretation_history.interpretation: crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes roughly doubling, from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to ~1200+/month (Aug 1180, Sep 1260), confirming the surge is real and sustained over two months rather than a single-month spike, but the data itself does not identify a cause.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning current ticket response handling is comfortably within SLA. This undercuts the premise that the surge is a response-handling/throughput gap, since tickets are being answered on time even as volume has doubled — the problem looks like it lies upstream in bill correctness, not in response speed.

billing-db shows 3025 disputed bills split by read type: 1785 tied to ACTUAL reads vs 1240 to ESTIMATED reads. The majority of disputes are therefore on bills built from accepted/actual reads, not from estimate substitution.

E-03 still shows 3025 disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED-read vs 1785 ACTUAL-read; that split and the ACTUAL-read dominance remain valid. It no longer supports that the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes stem from estimate substitution for missing manual reads: E-12 shows 1184 of those 1240 are AMI-channel reads that existed and were received before cutoff but were rejected at billing import under a HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule, so the ESTIMATED-read dispute slice is dominantly an import-validation failure, not a manual-read/route-completion-driven estimate substitution.

E-04 (billing-db.tariff_change_log) shows zero recorded tariff changes, ruling out a billing rate/tariff change as a cause of the dispute surge. It does not identify what actually caused the surge, so the leading hypotheses (bad read import, AMI handoff failure, or rule-change) remain open.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, a stakeholder, claims there has been no tariff change this year; this is a non-authoritative statement that merely echoes the already-recorded authoritative finding E-04 (billing-db tariff_change_log, zero records) and adds no new causal information about the dispute surge.

Route-log shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target over 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep, i.e. roughly 1,100 accounts with missed/incomplete manual reads. That gap is similar in size to the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-03), suggesting missed field routes could plausibly explain the estimated-read slice of disputes, but it says nothing about the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1,785, E-03) and does not itself establish staffing as the cause of the shortfall.

E-06 still shows Aug-Sep manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target over 9200 manual-read accounts (~1,100-account gap); that measurement remains valid. It no longer supports that this route-completion shortfall plausibly explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes: E-12 shows those disputes are dominantly (1184/1240) AMI-channel reads rejected at billing import under a HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule, not manual-read accounts affected by missed routes, so the numeric similarity between the ~1,100 route gap and the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes is coincidental, not causal.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three field readers since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers receive estimated bills; this is an unverified, non-authoritative stakeholder claim, not a tool observation, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) to attribute the surge to staffing. It offers a candidate cause for the ~1,100-account route completion gap already seen in E-06, but says nothing about why the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (E-03, 1,785 of 3,025) is disputed.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) states the utility may request route priority changes but these are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation; this is a governance/authority clarification matching the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint, not causal evidence about the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle returns 320 accounts (40 distinct routes) that were marked ESTIMATED in the most recent billing cycle, with sample account AC-20000 on route R-00. E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) identifies 14 specific routes with below-target completion rates (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), providing route-level granularity behind the aggregate 88% vs 95% completion gap already seen in E-06. It locates where the ESTIMATED-read-driving shortfall sits geographically but does not itself establish why those routes lag (staffing vs other field-ops causes).

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI, a vendor-side stakeholder, claims MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is an unverified stakeholder statement about data-access state, not a tool/document confirmation and not itself evidence about AMI read quality or the dispute-surge cause; it only suggests the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be retryable.

mdms-export's read-event query for the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (matching E-03) shows these are AMI-channel reads, not manual-read accounts: 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but REJECTED at import under a HIGH_CONSUMPTION validation rule, while only 56 genuinely had NO_READ_RECEIVED. This indicates the ESTIMATED-read dispute slice is dominantly caused by a billing import validation rule wrongly rejecting valid AMI reads, not by manual-read route-completion/staffing shortfalls as the problem definition's causal chain assumed, and it also confirms vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is now functioning.

mdms-export's firmware catalog (E-13) shows AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) report in register units of 0.1 m3 while older v3.x firmware reports in m3; if billing import does not correctly rescale v4.2 reads, their apparent consumption would read ~10x too high, which would trip the HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection seen in E-12 without any change to the validation rule itself.

E-14.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config's rule-change log shows BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling: none) was deployed 2026-08-01 — exactly at the Aug-Sep surge onset (E-01) — a rule that would misfire on v4.2-firmware meters whose raw register units are 0.1 m3 (E-13), explaining the HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections in E-12. The only other logged change, BV-09, is a 2026-03-02 label-text edit and predates the surge, so it is causally irrelevant.

U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the ACTUAL-read billing error caused by an AMI/MDMS handoff failure (H-AMI-HANDOFF-FAILURE), a billing import validation rule change (H-RULE-CHANGE), or both?
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must target the vendor AMI/MDMS handoff, the billing-config rule change, or both, before any bill-adjustment action can be scoped.
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-config.rule_change_log around August and mdms-export read events for disputed ACTUAL-read accounts once vendor access is provisioned.
U-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue manual, human-reviewed investigation and ticket handling; do not deploy any auto-fix or auto-answer agent until root cause is attributed.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.question: mdms-export is DEGRADED and a HOLD was issued (recovery_decision seq 88, ACCESS_PENDING) — when will vendor-provisioned access to AMI read events become available?
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.decision_impact: Blocks verification of the AMI-handoff-failure hypothesis and thus blocks root-cause attribution for the dominant ACTUAL-read dispute slice.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution_path: ORG-AMI vendor provisions MDMS export access per DA-MDMS acquisition requirement.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db and billing-config investigation in parallel; treat the AMI-handoff hypothesis as open.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution: mdms-export.read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned a COMPLETE, AUTHORITATIVE result (E-12), confirming vendor-provisioned export access is now available and the earlier access block is resolved.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-COUNTING-ARTIF.question: Does part of the doubling in dispute ticket volume (E-01) reflect a CRM categorization or counting change rather than new billing errors?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-COUNTING-ARTIF.decision_impact: If part of the doubling is a counting artifact, the M-DISPUTE-VOLUME target and urgency should be rescaled rather than treated as pure billing-error growth.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-COUNTING-ARTIF.resolution_path: Audit CRM ticket categorization/counting rules across Jun-Sep via audit_ticket_categorization:DA-TICKET.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-COUNTING-ARTIF.safe_placeholder: Treat the current M-DISPUTE-VOLUME reading as an upper bound on real billing-error growth pending the audit.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the nightly AMI read export handoff (H-MDMS-BILL) delivering completely and semantically validly for the ACTUAL-read population, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are currently UNKNOWN?
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If the nightly MDMS export handoff itself is unreliable, the mdms-export read-event query used to attribute ACTUAL-read disputes could be built on incomplete or invalid data, undermining SC-ROOT-CAUSE-SCOPE-DETERMINED.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Check H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity directly via mdms-export when running the ACTUAL-read query.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat mdms-export results for ACTUAL-read accounts as provisional and flag any root-cause attribution that relies on them until handoff validity is confirmed.

A-ACTUAL-READ-ERRORS-ARE-IMPOR.statement: The errors in ACTUAL-marked reads originate in the billing import/validation step or an upstream data source (AMI/MDMS or field feed), not in a shift of customer dispute behavior.

A-TICKET-COUNTING-UNCHANGED.statement: CRM ticket counting/categorization methodology was unchanged between Jun-Jul and Aug-Sep, so the volume increase in E-01 reflects real billing-error growth rather than a counting artifact.

A-STAFFING-LIMITED-TO-ESTIMATE.statement: Any field staffing shortfall at most explains the smaller ESTIMATED-read dispute slice (1240), not the larger ACTUAL-read slice (1785), which dominates the surge.

A-BV17-MECHANISM-SCOPE.statement: The 1184 accounts rejected under BV-17 (E-12) are assumed to be the firmware-v4.2 population described in E-13, since no evidence directly confirms firmware version on each rejected account.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets doubling since August and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01). Investigation (PD-1, now v2) found the real root cause: billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), misreads firmware-v4.2 AMI meters that report in 0.1 m3 units instead of m3 (E-13), inflating apparent consumption ~10x and wrongly rejecting valid reads as HIGH_CONSUMPTION. This explains 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (E-12, confirmed per-account by E-15/E-16); 56 others had genuinely no read received. Response-time throughput (E-02) and tariff changes (E-04) were ruled out as causes; initial field-staffing (CL-03/E-07) and AMI-handoff-failure hypotheses were investigated but contradicted by E-12. The requester's framing (auto-answer/auto-fix AI agent) was rejected (H-REQUESTER-FRAMING) since response times are within SLA and no automated bill writes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE). The release decision is HOLD, not a release: a critical verification obligation (VOB-R-5) about whether firmware version is confirmed per-account for BV-17-rejected accounts intersects the only release-scope deliverable (the BV-17 unit-scaling fix recommendation document). A verification pass also flagged a semantic inconsistency: the recorded limitations describe A-BV17-MECHANISM-SCOPE as still unconfirmed, but evidence E-15 and E-16 (two independent authoritative sources) directly confirm firmware v4.2 for all 1184 accounts and the confirming work item is marked DONE, so that stated limitation contradicts the cited evidence and needs correction before release.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1 v2): dispute volume roughly doubled Jun-Jul (~600/mo) to Aug-Sep (~1200+/mo, E-01), driven by BV-17's unscaled high-consumption check (deployed 2026-08-01, E-14) wrongly rejecting firmware-v4.2 AMI reads that report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13), causing 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts to be rejected (E-12).

Alternative causes were tested and ruled out or superseded: tariff change (E-04/E-05/CL-02=False), response-time bottleneck (E-02 within SLA), field-staffing shortfall (H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL REJECTED, contradicted by E-03/E-12 despite SH-FIELD's claim E-07/CL-03), and AMI-handoff failure (H-AMI-HANDOFF-FAILURE REJECTED, contradicted by E-12/E-14/E-16).

The original request (CL-01: build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills) was rejected as the solution path (H-REQUESTER-FRAMING REJECTED) because response times are within SLA (E-02) and automated bill writes are prohibited by constraint K-BILLWRITE.

The release scope is limited to one deliverable: a document recommending the BV-17 unit-scaling fix (document_recommended_bv17_unit_scaling_fix:DA-RULES); the actual engineering patch (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX) cannot be deployed in contest time.
Release decision is HOLD because open critical verification obligation VOB-R-5 (whether firmware version is confirmed per-account for BV-17-rejected accounts) intersects the release scope.
